Hello and thank you for offering to help.

You can check out this thread if you want to join ongoing efforts with redesign of all "default" subs.

If you want to have a go at redesigning whoaverse default style, you are welcome to do so, but I don't think we need to be fixing something that is not essentially broken. Minimalistic, simple, elegant, responsive and accessible is what we aim for. No fancy shadows, popup, rollover, slide in-out effects and alike as these only degrade usability aspect of the website. People usually have 10+ tabs open at any given time, and if whoaverse uses any effects which require more CPU/GPU power than google.com frontpage, people will not be happy about it. The site needs to be and feel as lightweight as possible and render blazing fast even on ancient devices and old browsers. That is a huge challenge. Digg style shows very little information at any given time and is not using screen real-estate in an optimal way. On my 22" screen, I can see only 4 submissions/articles on digg frontpage. Digg is the worst possible example you could use when redesigning whoaverse :)
